newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT-Newmont Mining raises Santa Fe bid.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-Newmont Mining raises Santa Fe bid.

text.p: Newmont Mining Corp said it raised its bid for Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp to 0.40 of a share of Newmont common for each Santa Fe share. A full text of its statement follows.
Newmont Mining Increases its Bid for Santa Fe 12.8% Over Homestake's Proposal

DENVER, Colo., Jan. 7 /PRNewswire/ -- Newmont Mining Corporation (NYSE: NEM) announced today that it has increased its offer for Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corporation (NYSE: GLD) to 0.40 of a share of Newmont common stock for each outstanding Santa Fe share. In a registration statement filed today with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Newmont said it intends to commence an exchange offer for each of Santa Fe's approximately 133 million outstanding common shares on a fully diluted basis.

Based on yesterday's closing price on the New York Stock Exchange, the Newmont proposal has a value of $16.50 per share of Santa Fe, or an aggregate value of approximately $2.2 billion. The offer represents a significant increase from Newmont's initial offer of 0.33 of a share made on December 5, 1996, 39% above Santa Fe's pre-offer price of December 4 and is 12.8% above Homestake Mining Company's offer of 1.115 Homestake shares for each share of Santa Fe, based on yesterday's closing prices.

Simultaneously, Newmont said its board of directors has requested that Santa Fe take all action necessary so that its shareholders can receive the benefits of the Newmont proposal, including entering into negotiations with Newmont in order to terminate Santa Fe's merger agreement with Homestake. In addition, Newmont said it is filing preliminary proxy materials with the SEC today to be used in connection with the solicitation of Santa Fe shareholders against the merger of Homestake and Santa Fe.

"The combination of our two companies is the best fit at the best price with unparalleled opportunities to create long-term value," said Ronald C. Cambre, Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer of Newmont. "It is clear that Santa Fe is for sale and a Newmont-Santa Fe combination offers not only a superior price today, but the best value for all shareholders tomorrow and into the next century."

Mr. Cambre continued, "Santa Fe's principal assets are two large mines in Nevada, and its extensive and largely unexplored property position in the state. Our combination would bring to Santa Fe the advantages of Newmont's global exploration capability and operating cost-efficiency. Our two companies would benefit both from the proximity of each company's Nevada properties and from their complementary proprietary technologies. These are synergies that Santa Fe cannot achieve either on its own or in combination with any other company."
